title: A dissociation between moral judgments and justifications
central_claims: Moral judgments follow double-effect distinctions across sampled demographics.
Most participants cannot justify the distinctions, suggesting judgment/introspection dissociation.

sources.title: A dissociation between moral judgments and justifications
sources.finding: Original text identifies broader thesis beyond the selected replication comparison.

sources.title: Many Labs 2: Investigating Variation in Replicability Across Samples and Settings
sources.finding: Trolley scenarios reproduce permissibility differences but do not test justification dissociation; original coauthors Cushman and Young are consortium authors.

sources.title: The Means/Side-Effect Distinction in Moral Cognition: A Meta-Analysis
sources.finding: Feltz and May include Hauser2007 experiments; aggregate difference persists but personal contact strongly moderates it.

search_log.purpose: Verify original thesis and read primary author text
Find claim-specific independent outcomes and contrary evidence
Inspect systematic synthesis and contrary contact-moderation evidence

search_gaps: Blind repeat: first researcher grades and drafts were not inspected.
A positive selected replication does not validate every central claim.
Downstream operational adoption and practical utility were not established.
summary: Permissibility differences recur, including a smaller no-contact contrast. Independent synthesis uses the results but emphasizes contact moderation. The central justification dissociation is not tested by ML2, so full-thesis validation remains unknown.
